_comment: Registry of event-listing surfaces -- the free discovery channels a SparkDate event should appear on, plus the ones deliberately NOT pursued and why. scripts/build-listing-pack.js reads this to generate per-site copy and UTM'd links; .claude/commands/syndicate-events.md reads it to drive the browser. Add a site HERE, not in a runbook paragraph, so the generator and the driver both pick it up.

_evidence._comment: Why the statuses below say what they say. Source: Night Tasks/ga4-api-traffic-by-source-2026-09-01.csv, window 2026-05-19 to 2026-09-01. Re-derive before trusting; these numbers age.
_evidence.eventbrite_listing: 170 sessions / 81 users / 23 key events / $290.39 -- the highest revenue of any source except (direct), and the ONLY event-listing surface producing anything at all.
_evidence.patch_referral: 1 session, 0 key events. It is in the hand-kept UTM sheet, so it was planned; it was never actually worked.
_evidence.nextdoor_cpc: 22 sessions, 1 key event -- and it is PAID. The free Nextdoor Events post is a different surface and has never been used.
_evidence.everything_else: Zero. No meetup, no allevents, no discoverlancaster, no lancasteronline, no facebook.com/events organic, no google business. Free listing discovery is currently a one-legged stool.
_evidence._the_headline: One free channel carries the entire non-paid, non-direct funnel. That is the risk this registry exists to spread.

_utm._comment: The convention is not invented here -- `eventbrite / listing` already exists in GA4 and converts, so the rest of the surfaces are shaped to match it and land in the same report.
_utm._medium_why: Deliberately NOT 'referral'. GA4 assigns 'referral' by itself to any uncontrolled inbound link, so a hand-tagged listing would drown in it. 'listing' is a bucket nothing else writes to, which makes 'what did free event calendars do for us' a single readable row.
_utm._campaign_why: Matches content/brand.json universal.utm.campaign_format. The old 'week3_Solution' shape went stale by construction every month.
_utm._content_why: Unique per listing per event, so one calendar's performance is separable from another's. brand.json bans a shared utm_content for exactly this reason (the 'proof_rsa1' defect on 11 ads).
_utm._destination_why: The event page, not /lp. Someone clicking 'tickets' from a calendar listing has already been sold the event -- /lp has no cart and would add a hop. See brand.json universal.landing_page_warning.
_utm._never_both: One UTM set per link. If a site rewrites or wraps outbound links (Facebook, Nextdoor), verify the tags survive the wrapper before counting on the row.

sites.name: Eventbrite
sites.cost: free to list; ticket fees only on paid sales
sites.notes: Already the primary. Also the checkout for a large share of sales, which is why its buyers need the manual /admin Enroll step -- docs/EVENTBRITE_ENROLLMENT.md.
gotchas: Eventbrite buyers do NOT get a SparkDate account or chemistry profile automatically.
GA4 cannot see Eventbrite-side purchases at all -- see the ga4-revenue-is-own-site-only memory. Its listing sessions are visible; its checkout is not.

sites.name: Facebook Event (from the SparkDate Page)
sites.why_now: The account already runs paid Facebook and has the Page, the audience and the creative. A Page Event is the same asset posted to a surface that costs nothing, and every RSVP is shown to that person's friends -- the one channel here with built-in amplification. GA4 shows zero organic Facebook event traffic, so this is unworked ground, not a saturated one.
gotchas: Facebook wraps outbound links. Confirm the utm_* params survive the l.facebook.com hop before trusting the GA4 row -- 53 sessions already land as 'm.facebook.com / referral' with no campaign attached.
An Event is distinct from a post about the event. Both are worth doing; only the Event gets RSVPs and reminders.

sites.name: Discover Lancaster (official county tourism)
sites.why_now: The highest-authority local calendar in the county and the one that ranks for 'things to do in Lancaster'. Named in docs/MARKETING_PLAYBOOK.md in June 2026 and still never submitted.

constraints.image: 600x600, no logos and no words in the image

gotchas: Submit at least two weeks ahead or it will not clear moderation in time.
Check the calendar for an existing duplicate before submitting; they ask for this explicitly.

sites.name: LancasterOnline / LNP calendar
sites.why_now: The local paper's calendar. High local trust and indexed by Google, which is the point -- 'singles events Lancaster PA' currently returns nothing of ours.
gotchas: The submit flow is inside the calendar app itself (a #! route), not a separate /submit page. Open the calendar and find the submit control on the page rather than guessing a URL.

sites.name: LancasterPA.com

constraints.image: max 705x300, under 1 MB (larger files are auto-deleted)

gotchas: Editorially screened -- they publish only what suits their audience.
The outbound link back to our site is stated as a courtesy for current customers; do not assume the link renders. Verify the live listing after approval.

sites.name: Visit Lancaster PA
gotchas: The old /Lancaster-County/Event-Calendar/Submit-an-Event/ path in MARKETING_PLAYBOOK.md now redirects here. Use this URL.

sites.name: Visit Lancaster City
sites.why_now: Downtown-specific, which is exactly where the venues are. Marion Court Room and Tellus360 are both city-centre rooms.

sites.name: Fig Lancaster
sites.why_now: Local lifestyle brand with the closest audience fit of the tourism calendars -- their readers are the people who go out on a weeknight.

sites.name: Lancaster Chamber community calendar
gotchas: Some chamber calendars restrict submissions to members. Check before spending time on the form; if members-only, mark it rejected rather than leaving it in the queue forever.

sites.name: AllEvents.in
sites.cost: free to list; paid only for extra visibility
sites.why_now: Aggregator with real search presence for '<city> events' queries and a genuinely free listing tier. Cheap to maintain because it will also ingest an Eventbrite listing.
gotchas: It may auto-import the Eventbrite listing. Check for an existing auto-imported copy first and claim/edit that instead of creating a duplicate.
An auto-imported listing carries EVENTBRITE's link, not a UTM'd one -- claiming it is what lets the tag be set.

sites.name: Patch — Lancaster PA
sites.why_now: Already in the hand-kept UTM sheet and has produced exactly 1 session ever, which means it was planned and then dropped rather than tried and rejected. Low cost to revive.
gotchas: The community slug is `lancaster-pa`, not `lancaster` -- the bare slug 404s.

sites.name: Nextdoor — free Events post
sites.why_now: Nextdoor is ALREADY being paid for (22 sessions at cpc). The free Events post is a separate surface on the same account and has never been used.
gotchas: Requires a logged-in neighbourhood account; the events URL bounces to login.
Keep utm_source distinct from the paid Nextdoor traffic or the free post's contribution is unreadable.

sites.name: Meetup — our own SparkDate group
sites.cost: already paid for — the group exists and has sold tickets
sites.role: discovery + a standing audience we already own
sites.why_now: CORRECTED 2026-09-02. This was recorded as 'rejected -- fails the free-only constraint', on the assumption that using Meetup meant buying a subscription first. Taylor already has the group and has already sold 2 tickets through it, so the subscription is a sunk cost and posting there is now among the cheapest listings on this list. About 20 members sit in it, unworked.
gotchas: The 2 tickets it has sold appear NOWHERE in GA4 and carry no attribution on any attendee record -- they went through Meetup's own checkout, the same blind spot Eventbrite has. Do not judge this channel by what the dashboard shows.
Member emails are NOT obtainable on a standard organizer plan. Only Meetup Pro can export them, and even then only for members who RSVP'd AND consented to share. Do not plan around getting the list.
Because the list cannot be extracted, the event post itself has to carry the signup CTA -- that is how a Meetup member becomes a SparkDate member with real consent, rather than a scraped address.

sites.name: Meetup — other people's local singles groups
sites.rejected_reason: Someone else's group. Posting a ticketed event into one uninvited is how you get removed, and it is a conversation with a human organizer rather than a form to fill. docs/MARKETING_PLAYBOOK.md identified 'South Central PA (SOLO) Singles' (meetup.com/meetup-group-pujqfyel) in June 2026; it stays a manual ask, not a syndication target.
sites.reconsider_if: An organizer says yes. Then it is a one-off post, not a recurring channel.

sites.name: Google Business Profile — Events post
sites.role: discovery on branded and near-me search
sites.why_now: `googlebusinessposting` is already a row in the hand-kept UTM sheet, so it was intended. GA4 has never recorded a session from it. Free, and it surfaces on the exact 'singles events near me' searches nothing of ours currently answers.
gotchas: PRECONDITION: confirm a verified Google Business Profile actually exists for SparkDate before planning around this. A business with no fixed public address has to be set up as a service-area business, and verification takes time. If there is no profile, the first task is creating one, not posting to one.
Event posts expire after the event date -- this is a per-event chore, not a set-and-forget.

sites.name: Events.org
sites.why_now: Low expected traffic. Worth one submission for the backlink, not worth a recurring slot.
gotchas: Judge this one on whether it is still indexed at all before repeating it. Aggregators in this tier go stale quietly.

sites.name: Ticket Tailor
sites.cost: $0.85/ticket pay-as-you-sell (~$0.30 prepaid), plus our own Stripe; free for free events
sites.role: indexable public event page + a cheaper box office than Eventbrite
sites.why_now: Taylor's call 2026-09-02, after the reasoning below was corrected. The honest value is an indexed event page carrying schema.org Event markup, NOT discovery and NOT fees.
sites._correction: This entry previously said 'rejected' and offered a reconsider_if: 'as a fee play against Eventbrite it is a real option'. THAT WAS WRONG, and it was wrong because it compared Ticket Tailor to Eventbrite instead of to what we already own. Fees per $24.99 ticket: Eventbrite ~$3.43 (3.7% + $1.79 service, plus 2.9% processing), Ticket Tailor ~$1.87 ($0.85 + Stripe), sparkdate.date ~$1.02 (Stripe alone). We already run a Stripe checkout in public/event.html, so ANY third-party box office is more expensive than our own. The fee play is moving volume from Eventbrite to our own site, not adding a platform.
sites._why_not_discovery: Ticket Tailor has no marketplace. Nobody browses it. Eventbrite's fees buy exactly one thing we cannot replicate -- a consumer marketplace that produced 170 sessions and 23 key events unprompted -- which is why Eventbrite stays despite costing 3x.
gotchas: It is a THIRD checkout after sparkdate.date and Eventbrite. Every checkout is another place price, date and capacity drift out of sync -- the failure this repo spent 2026-09-01 unpicking, when one event had four different end times across five surfaces.

Buyers there will need the same manual /admin Enroll step Eventbrite buyers need (docs/EVENTBRITE_ENROLLMENT.md). They arrive with no account and no chemistry profile, and the seating tool cannot put someone at a table without one.
Payment runs through our own Stripe and connecting it is an account action. Do not publish a sellable event before that is done -- a live page with broken checkout is worse than no page.
Judge this one on whether its event pages actually emit schema.org Event JSON-LD. That is the entire case for it; without it there is no reason to keep it.

sites.name: Visit PA (state tourism)
sites.role: discovery + the strongest SEO backlink on this list
sites.why_now: State-level tourism board, higher domain authority than any county calendar here, and nothing of ours is on it. Verified live 2026-09-02.
gotchas: The submission path is NOT /submit-event/ -- that 404s. Find it from the events page itself.
State tourism boards moderate for tourist relevance. A weeknight singles mixer may not fit their editorial line; if it is rejected, record that here rather than retrying each event.

sites.name: Facebook — local singles groups
sites.role: community posting into the closest audience match available
sites.why_now: docs/MARKETING_PLAYBOOK.md named three Lancaster singles groups in June 2026 and none was ever worked. 'Lancaster Area Singles Mingles' verified live 2026-09-02. Best audience fit of anything on this list.
gotchas: NOT a form to fill. These are other people's groups with their own rules, and a listing-shaped post reads as spam and gets removed -- same reason reddit_lancaster is out_of_scope. It needs hand-written copy and a read of the group's promo rules first.
Distinct from `facebook_event`, which is our own Page's Event. Do both; they reach different people.
Facebook wraps outbound links. Confirm the utm_ parameters survive the l.facebook.com hop before trusting any GA4 row -- the short link exists partly for this.

sites.name: Yelp for Business — Events
sites.why_now: Free, and it posts events from a business page.
gotchas: PRECONDITION: there must be a claimed SparkDate Yelp business page first. Events post FROM a business page, so with no page this is a page-claiming job, not a listing job. Check before planning around it.
Same shape of precondition as google_business. If neither profile exists, do them together -- it is one afternoon of identity setup that unblocks two channels.

sites.name: Eventful.com
sites.rejected_reason: Dead. Audacy folded it into radio.com in 2021 and the domain no longer resolves. It still appears in most 'free event listing sites' roundups, which is how stale advice keeps propagating -- recorded here so it does not get re-suggested.

sites.name: Reddit — r/lancaster
sites.rejected_reason: Free and a real local audience, but it is a community, not a listing surface -- a form-filled event post reads as spam there and most local subs remove promotional posts outright. It belongs in the organic-social workflow with hand-written copy, not in an automated syndication run.
sites.see: docs/MARKETING_PLAYBOOK.md section 5 has the human-voiced draft.

philadelphia_when_active._comment: No Philadelphia event is currently on sale -- Good Good Things was 2026-08-31. Parked until there is a Philly date; re-verify before use.
